passages.text: And the LORD said to Job: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Job.
The LORD said these words.
God is Almighty.
A person who finds fault cannot contend with the Almighty.
Anyone who argues with God must answer Him.
passages.original: וַיַּ֖עַן יְהוָ֥ה אֶת־ אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ הֲ֭רֹב עִם־ שַׁדַּ֣י יִסּ֑וֹר מוֹכִ֖יחַ אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַעֲנֶֽנָּה׃פ

passages.text: Then Job answered the LORD: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.
passages.sermon:
Job spoke to the LORD.
Job said, "I am insignificant.
I cannot answer You.
I put my hand over my mouth."
passages.original: וַיַּ֖עַן אִיּ֥וֹב אֶת־ יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ הֵ֣ן קַ֭לֹּתִי מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶ֑ךָּ יָ֝דִ֗י שַׂ֣מְתִּי לְמוֹ־ פִֽי׃

passages.text: I have spoken once, but I have no answer— twice, but I have nothing to add.”
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffered greatly.
Job spoke to the LORD.
Job said, "I spoke once."
I have no answer.
I spoke a second time.
I have nothing more to add.
passages.original: אַחַ֣ת דִּ֭בַּרְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה וּ֝שְׁתַּ֗יִם וְלֹ֣א אוֹסִֽיף׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Job.
The LORD spoke from the whirlwind.
The LORD said to Job, "Prepare yourself like a man.
I will ask you questions.
You will answer Me."
passages.original: וַיַּֽעַן־ יְהוָ֣ה אֶת־ אִ֭יּוֹב מִנ סְעָרָה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ אֱזָר־ נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job a question.
God says, “Would you cancel My justice?
Would you declare Me guilty?
Would you do this so that you can be right?”
passages.original: הַ֭אַף תָּפֵ֣ר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י תַּ֝רְשִׁיעֵ֗נִי לְמַ֣עַן תִּצְדָּֽק׃

passages.text: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Job from the whirlwind.
God is powerful and mighty.
God asked Job a question.
God said, “Do you have an arm like God?”
God said, “Can you thunder with a voice like God?”
passages.original: וְאִם־ זְר֖וֹעַ כָּאֵ֥ל׀ לָ֑ךְ וּ֝בְק֗וֹל כָּמֹ֥הוּ תַרְעֵֽם׃

passages.text: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God is powerful and just.
God asks Job a question.
God says, “Put on majesty and greatness.
Wear honor and glory as your clothing.”
passages.original: עֲדֵ֥ה נָ֣א גָֽא֣וֹן וָגֹ֑בַהּ וְה֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר תִּלְבָּֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God is all-powerful.
God commands Job.
Release your anger.
Look at every proud person.
Humble each proud person.
passages.original: הָ֭פֵץ עֶבְר֣וֹת אַפֶּ֑ךָ וּרְאֵ֥ה כָל־ גֵּ֝אֶ֗ה וְהַשְׁפִּילֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God is all-powerful.
God commands Job to look at every proud person.
God tells Job to humble every proud person.
God commands Job to trample the wicked.
God tells Job to bring the wicked down where they stand.
passages.original: רְאֵ֣ה כָל־ גֵּ֭אֶה הַכְנִיעֵ֑הוּ וַהֲדֹ֖ךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃

passages.text: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.
passages.sermon: God commands action against the wicked.\r\nBury the wicked together in the dust.\r\nImprison their faces in the grave.
passages.original: טָמְנֵ֣ם בֶּעָפָ֣ר יָ֑חַד פְּ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם חֲבֹ֣שׁ בַּטָּמֽוּן׃

passages.text: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God says, “If you can humble every proud person,
If you can crush the wicked where they stand,
If you can bury them all in the dust,
If you can imprison them in the grave,
Then I will admit this to you.
I will say your own right hand can save you.”
passages.original: וְגַם־ אֲנִ֥י אוֹדֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־ תוֹשִׁ֖עַ לְךָ֣ יְמִינֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God says, “Look at Behemoth.
I made Behemoth when I made you.
Behemoth eats grass.
He eats grass like an ox.”
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ נָ֣א בְ֭הֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂ֣יתִי עִמָּ֑ךְ חָ֝צִ֗יר כַּבָּקָ֥ר יֹאכֵֽל׃

passages.text: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.
passages.sermon:
Behemoth is a creature God made.
Behemoth has strong loins.
Behemoth has powerful muscles in his belly.
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ נָ֣א כֹח֣וֹ בְמָתְנָ֑יו וְ֝אֹנ֗וֹ בִּשְׁרִירֵ֥י בִטְנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
passages.sermon:
Behemoth is a great creature that God made.
\r\nBehemoth has a tail.
\r\nHis tail moves like a cedar tree.
\r\nBehemoth has strong thighs.
\r\nThe sinews in his thighs are tightly bound together.
passages.original: יַחְפֹּ֣ץ זְנָב֣וֹ כְמוֹ־ אָ֑רֶז גִּידֵ֖י פַחֲדוֹ יְשֹׂרָֽגוּ׃

passages.text: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.
passages.sermon: This creature is very strong.\r\nHis bones are like tubes made of bronze.\r\nHis limbs are like rods made of iron.
passages.original: עֲ֭צָמָיו אֲפִיקֵ֣י נְחוּשָׁ֑ה גְּ֝רָמָ֗יו כִּמְטִ֥יל בַּרְזֶֽל׃

passages.text: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.
passages.sermon: This creature is the foremost of God’s works.\r\nGod made him.\r\nOnly God, his Maker, can approach him with a sword.
passages.original: ה֭וּא רֵאשִׁ֣ית דַּרְכֵי־ אֵ֑ל הָ֝עֹשׂוֹ יַגֵּ֥שׁ חַרְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.
passages.sermon: Behemoth is a powerful creature made by God.\r\nThe hills give Behemoth their produce.\r\nAll the wild animals play near Behemoth.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ ב֭וּל הָרִ֣ים יִשְׂאוּ־ ל֑וֹ וְֽכָל־ חַיַּ֥ת הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה יְשַֽׂחֲקוּ־ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.
passages.sermon:
Behemoth is a powerful creature.
God created Behemoth as the foremost of His works.
Behemoth lies under the lotus plants.
He hides among the reeds of the marsh.
passages.original: תַּֽחַת־ צֶאֱלִ֥ים יִשְׁכָּ֑ב בְּסֵ֖תֶר קָנֶ֣ה וּבִצָּֽה׃

passages.text: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.
passages.sermon:
Behemoth is a great and powerful creature.
\r\nLotus plants grow near him.
\r\nThe shade of the lotus plants hides Behemoth.
\r\nWillows grow by the brook.
\r\nThe willows surround Behemoth.
passages.original: יְסֻכֻּ֣הוּ צֶאֱלִ֣ים צִֽלֲל֑וֹ יְ֝סֻבּ֗וּהוּ עַרְבֵי־ נָֽחַל׃

passages.text: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.
passages.sermon:
Behemoth is a great and powerful creature.
A river may rage and flood.
Behemoth does not fear the river.
He stays calm and unafraid.
Even if the Jordan River rushes to his mouth, he remains secure.
The river’s power does not disturb him.
Behemoth trusts in his own strength.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן יַעֲשֹׁ֣ק נָ֭הָר לֹ֣א יַחְפּ֑וֹז יִבְטַ֓ח׀ כִּֽי־ יָגִ֖יחַ יַרְדֵּ֣ן אֶל־ פִּֽיהוּ׃

passages.text: Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?
passages.sermon:
Behemoth is a powerful and fearless creature.
No one can capture Behemoth while he watches.
No one can pierce Behemoth’s nose with a snare.
passages.original: בְּעֵינָ֥יו יִקָּחֶ֑נּוּ בְּ֝מֽוֹקְשִׁ֗ים יִנְקָב־ אָֽף׃
